chapter: Postwar years, accident and lean times
title: End of Tape Eight: scheduling and goodbyes; Part IV begins May 5, 1975
summary: Wilson sets the next session, declines dinner and leaves his phone number; the tape ends and Part IV opens on May 5, 1975.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing the interview: thanks, goodbyes and tape running out

blocks.x: : Well we're coming -- we're coming, Herman, to the end of this reel.
Okay.
: And I think next time we'll pick up with Red Richards, how you met Red -- well, we've talked about that, but the beginning of your relationship with Red.
All right.
: And going to Europe, and we'll do all that. Okay?
Uh-huh. Okay.
: Fine.
Okay, thanks a lot.
: Uh, now, let's see. I've got to go now. But for the next time -- now where are we now? Thursday. How is Monday of next week?
All right.
Is that okay with you?
Yeah, so far.--
Same time?
Yeah, so far I don't know anything --
Okay. You know, one thing I've got to give you is my phone number --
Oh, please! Thank you.
In case something happens and you're not going to be able to make it.
Well all right, I'll write it -- thank you. I'll write it down here. I have plenty of junk I can write it on, (unintelligible).
Tear this off and give it to you. I'll give you my home phone, because that's where I normally am.
All right.
And if I'm not there, my wife is usually there, so --
Oh, all right. I'm glad we -- I've been trying every day -- my wife say did you ask? Did you ask? Would you like to stay for dinner?
Herman, thank you very much, I appreciate it, but the reason I have to go --
I know, but I mean --

The reason I have to go is because I've got to get downtown and do a couple of things that are trying to tape a radio show, and meet a guy for dinner, so -- (laughs.) But thank you very much. Some time I hope we'll be able to do it.
Well, we got to -- we've got to -- even if it's after we start on the book, or something. We've got -- we'll get together, okay?
Okay.
And you -- I want you to know you're welcome.
Well thank you. (Laughs.)
You're a cagy sort of guy, and you can ask me. Ask me, or tell me, well I'm staying for dinner. (Laughs.)
Thank you very much.
You know me, so I want you to know just how much you're welcome.
(Recording interruption.)
That poor thing, that's why she gets hurt so much. She's -- she's so crazy about people, and helping this one, helping that one, she gets it right in the teeth, every time.
Oh really?
Yeah, she's helped so many people, and
There must have been some of them that didn't kick her in the teeth.
We-e-1-1 -- a couple, maybe. But most, you know.
(End of Tape eight.)
